complexity_scope.guarantee: For every covered deterministic method and target t there exists a rotated hard instance satisfying the displayed bound.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Displayed constants are explicit. No extra uniformity in independently prescribed radii or stronger Oracles is inferred.
complexity_scope.oracle: One exact bundled query returns (grad f(x),Ax,A^T y). Public theta may include X,Y,g,b,Lf and the norm. Explicit access to the full unknown f or A, Hessian queries and other stronger feedback are not covered.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: A feasible approximate pair in X times Y, measured by phi(xbar^(t))-psi(ybar^(t)); output need not equal the latest query.
complexity_scope.regime: Iteration-dependent dimension restriction and coupled radius calibration stated above; no arbitrary-radius rescaling is claimed.
complexity_scope.resource: t is the output index in Eq. (8): output t is produced from replies at query indices 0 through t-1. Each reply bundles three components; this is not a count of separately available gradient/matrix-product calls. Arithmetic, projection and public-data processing are not separately bounded here.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: All deterministic adaptive methods of Eq. (8), including nonlinear query and feasible output rules; no span assumption or randomized lifting.

(14)-(15) give ||B||<=2 and ||Lambda||=2. Eq. (48) specifies H=(Lf/4)diag(B^T B,I), h=(Lf/4+LA/(4sqrt(2)))e_{2k,n}, A=(LA/2)Lambda and b=(LA/2)c; f(x)=x^T Hx/2-h^T x.

Krylov structure: Eq. (19) defines Ji=span{c,(Lambda Lambda^T)c,...,(Lambda Lambda^T)^i c}, Ki=Lambda^T Ji. Lemmas 2-3 and Eqs. (26)-(30) identify Ki=span{e_{2k-i,n},...,e_{2k,n}} and the nested information spaces. Eq. (42) gives ||Ax-b||^2>=k LA^2/4 on K_{k-1}.

Objective estimate: Lemma 9, pp.15-16, gives x*=(1,2,...,2k,0,...,0), a dual vector with first 2k entries -1/(2sqrt(2)), norm sqrt(k)/2, and optimal value -(Lf/4+LA/(2sqrt(2)))k. Lemma 10's Proof, pp.17-18, reduces f on K_{k-1} to a k-dimensional quadratic; Eq. (57) gives its minimum as -k(Lf+sqrt(2)LA+LA^2/(2Lf))/8.

The separate local-complete proof below extends the induction through that endpoint and proves transcript and output preservation explicitly; it is not a claimed source correction.

Proposition 3, pp.27-28, applies this rotation to the minus-sign saddle representation (83), using P(theta;U^T HU,-V^T AU), theta=(h,-b,X,Y,0). Rotationally invariant balls preserve feasibility, norms and optimal value; Eq. (86) transfers the primal gap to the minimum over K_{k-1} when 2t+3<=k-1.

proofs.full_local_argument:
Status and scope. This is a Curator-supplied local argument, not text attributed to the authors or an independent review. Fix the statement's m,n,t,Lf,LA and method M, and write T=t, k=2T+4 (an even integer at least 6). Then 2k<m<=n. All spaces use Euclidean norms. The construction and rotations below are for this one fixed T; no stronger simultaneous-instance quantifier is needed.

Construction. Put G=2[I_{m-2k},0] in R^{(m-2k) by (n-2k)}. Define B in R^{2k by 2k} by Bu=(u_{2k}-u_{2k-1},u_{2k-1}-u_{2k-2},...,u_2-u_1,u_1). Let Lambda=diag(B,G), c=(1_{2k},0), A0=(LA/2)Lambda, b0=(LA/2)c, H=(Lf/4)diag(B^T B,I_{n-2k}), alpha=Lf/4+LA/(4sqrt(2)), h=alpha e_{2k,n}, and f0(x)=x^T Hx/2-h^T x. B is invertible (successive differences determine u), and ||Bu||^2<=4||u||^2. Thus H is positive definite and ||H||<=Lf, while ||Lambda||=2 and ||A0||=LA, including LA=0. Let X and Y be the balls in R^n and R^m of radii RX=sqrt(k)(2k+1), RY=sqrt(k)/2. Initially use the minus-sign function L0(x,y)=f0(x)+<b0-A0x,y>. Its realization as Eq.(1) has coefficient C0=-A0 and public vector d=-b0. The final problem keeps this same plus-sign convention: fR(x)+<CR x-d,y>, with CR=-V^T A0 U. Its public b is d, not b0.

Subspaces needed, without unverified transfer. For 0<=i<=k-1 define Ki=span{e_{2k-i,n},...,e_{2k,n}} and Ji=span{c,e_{1,m},...,e_{i,m}} (J0=span{c}). The first 2k entries of c are all one, so these spaces have dimension i+1 and are strictly nested in this range. Direct multiplication of B gives B1=e_{2k}, Be_{2k}=e_1, and Be_j=e_{2k-j+1}-e_{2k-j} for j<2k; B is symmetric. Hence Lambda Ki=span{e_1,...,e_{i+1}} subset J_{i+1}, and Lambda^T Ji=Ki. These are precisely the Krylov spaces of Eq.(19): start at c and alternate Lambda^T and Lambda, obtaining the stated bases inductively. B^T B is tridiagonal (the quadratic form is u_1^2+sum_{j=2}^{2k}(u_j-u_{j-1})^2). Therefore HKi subset K_{i+1} whenever i+1<=k-1; also h belongs to K0 and c belongs to J0. These facts supply every containment used below.

Orthogonal extension fact. If E is a proper subspace of F in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, any v admits an orthogonal map Q fixing E pointwise with Qv in F. Write v=vE+w, w perpendicular to E. If w=0 take the identity; otherwise choose a unit a in F intersect E-perp and take an orthogonal map on E-perp sending w/||w|| to a, extended by identity on E. Such a map exists by extending each unit vector to an orthonormal basis. Its transpose also fixes E. This proves the rotation-existence input rather than treating a reference to Lemma 11 as a missing local step.

Oracle preservation calculation. Suppose U,V are orthogonal, Uh=h, Vc=c, and all previously queried x,y belong to U^T K_{2s-1}, V^T J_{2s-1}. Choose orthogonal Phi,Psi fixing E=U^T K_{2s}, F=V^T J_{2s} pointwise. Set U'=U Phi,V'=V Psi. For each such x,y, Phi x=x and Psi y=y. The vectors U^T H Ux, V^T A0 Ux and U^T A0^T Vy lie respectively in E,F,E by the preceding containments, so Phi^T or Psi^T on their corresponding outputs leaves them fixed. Consequently U'^T H U'x=U^T H Ux, V'^T A0 U'x=V^T A0 Ux, and U'^T A0^T V'y=U^T A0^T Vy. The identical equalities hold for the negative coefficients C=-V^T A0U and C'=-V'^T A0U'. Because U h=h implies h in U^T K0 subset E, Phi h=h; similarly Psi c=c. Thus U'h=h, V'c=c, and the full gradient H_R x-h and both signed matrix products are unchanged. The public vector d, balls, g=0, norm, Lf, and even h if supplied as additional public data are unchanged. Orthogonal rotations preserve the balls, so feasibility and all public side information in this model are consistent. No stronger Oracle giving explicit H or C is covered.

Inclusive induction and transcript. The initial query is fixed by M and the common public data. Apply the extension fact to K0 proper subset K1 and J0 proper subset J1 to choose U0,V0 fixing K0,J0 and taking x^(0),y^(0) into K1,J1. They fix h,c. Assume after stage s-1 that M on the rotated instance has numerical queries i=0,...,s-1 in U_{s-1}^T K_{2s-1},V_{s-1}^T J_{2s-1}. Run that instance to obtain its next query (x^(s),y^(s)). For every 1<=s<=T, including s=T, we have 2s<=k-4, 2s+1<=k-3, and s<=k/2. Thus K_{2s} is a proper subspace of K_{2s+1}, and J_{2s} is a proper subspace of J_{2s+1}; all required indices lie in the proved range. The extension fact chooses Phi,Psi fixing U_{s-1}^T K_{2s},V_{s-1}^T J_{2s} and placing Phi x^(s),Psi y^(s) in U_{s-1}^T K_{2s+1},V_{s-1}^T J_{2s+1}. Put Us=U_{s-1}Phi, Vs=V_{s-1}Psi. The preceding preservation calculation applies to every query i<s. Starting with the same initial query, induction on i shows that the replies at i=0,...,s-1 on the new instance equal those on the old instance: deterministic Eq.(8) then gives the same next query and output after each reply. In particular query s and output s are unchanged as numerical vectors. The earlier queries remain in the new transformed K_{2s-1},J_{2s-1} because Phi,Psi fixed them, and the new query is in the new transformed K_{2s+1},J_{2s+1} by construction. This completes the induction through s=T; it explicitly supplies the endpoint omitted by the strict printed induction. No step requires s<T.

Final output rotation. At stage T, all queries through T lie in UT^T K_{2T+1},VT^T J_{2T+1}. Take the numerical output (xbar^(T),ybar^(T)) of this instance (for T>=1 it is determined by replies 0,...,T-1). Since 2T+3=k-1, strict nesting still holds from indices 2T+2=k-2 to 2T+3=k-1. Choose Phi,Psi fixing UT^T K_{2T+2},VT^T J_{2T+2} and mapping the respective output vectors into UT^T K_{2T+3},VT^T J_{2T+3}. Set U=UT Phi,V=VT Psi. Use the Oracle-preservation calculation with s=T+1: s=(k-2)/2<=k/2 and the required H K_{2T+1} subset K_{2T+2} is within range. It preserves all three Oracle replies at every query through T. By the same deterministic transcript induction, the numerical outputs at index T, as well as these queries, remain identical. Also Uh=h and Vc=c. The final output satisfies U xbar^(T) in K_{2T+3}=K_{k-1}; feasible outputs require no span assumption. The dual output could likewise be placed in J_{k-1}, but the bound only needs its feasibility.

Transfer and optimum. Define fR(x)=f0(Ux), AR=V^T A0U, and LR(x,y)=fR(x)+<b0-ARx,y>, equivalently the original plus-sign model with CR=-AR and d=-b0. Because Vb0=b0, LR(x,y)=L0(Ux,Vy). Rotations map X,Y bijectively to themselves, so phiR(x)=phi0(Ux), phiR*=phi0*, and the spectral budgets remain ||CR||=LA and Lipschitz constant at most Lf. This proves the precise Proposition 3 transfer needed here without silently transferring a different version or Oracle.

Calibrated primal estimate. Put x*=(1,2,...,2k,0,...,0) and y*=-(1/(2sqrt(2)))(1_{2k},0). Then A0x*=b0, Hx*-h=A0^T y*, ||y*||=RY, and ||x*||^2=k(2k+1)(4k+1)/3<=RX^2. Therefore the convex function x -> L0(x,y*) has zero gradient at x*, while L0(x*,y) is constant for all y. Hence (x*,y*) is a saddle point on X times Y, and phi0*=f0(x*)=-(Lf/4+LA/(2sqrt(2)))k. These identities hold also at LA=0 without division by LA.

For x in K_{k-1}, write x=(0_k,z,0), z in R^k. The last k entries among the first 2k entries of A0x are zero, whereas each corresponding entry of b0 is LA/2. Thus ||A0x-b0||>=LA sqrt(k)/2. Also f0(x)=(Lf/8)[z_1^2+sum_{j=2}^k(z_j-z_{j-1})^2]-alpha z_k. Setting z0=0 and w_j=z_j-z_{j-1} makes z_k=sum w_j, so completing each square gives min_z f0(x)=-2k alpha^2/Lf=-(k/8)(Lf+sqrt(2)LA+LA^2/(2Lf)). Because Y is the Euclidean ball, phi0(x)=f0(x)+RY||A0x-b0||. Subtracting phi0* and combining both bounds yields phi0(x)-phi0* >= (k/8)(Lf+sqrt(2)LA-LA^2/(2Lf))+LA k/4. With 0<=LA<=Lf, this is at least Lf k/16+(sqrt(2)+2)LA k/8. This holds in particular on X intersect K_{k-1}; minimizing over the larger subspace in the intermediate quadratic bound is legitimate.

Conclusion. The final feasible output has U xbar^(T) in X intersect K_{k-1}. Transfer gives phiR(xbar^(T))-phiR* >= Lf k/16+(sqrt(2)+2)LA k/8. Weak duality gives psiR(ybar^(T))<=phiR* for its feasible dual output. Finally RX^2=k(2k+1)^2, RX RY=k(2k+1)/2 and 2k+1=4T+9 rewrite this exactly as the stated gap bound. This proves the originally assigned calibrated scope, including LA=0, and introduces neither arbitrary radii nor randomized or stronger-Oracle coverage.

assumptions: m,n,t are positive integers with 8<m<=n and 1<=t<m/4-2, hence k=2t+4<m/2.

M is a deterministic method described by Eq. (8), starting from an initial feasible query pair and choosing feasible query and output pairs from public theta and prior exact bundled Oracle replies (grad f(x),Ax,A^T y). Arbitrary deterministic nonlinear rules are allowed; no linear-span assumption is required.
The hard instance is existential and may depend on M and the target iteration t. The radii are those of Eq. (88), not freely independent inputs.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Consider min_{x in X} max_{y in Y} f(x)+<Ax-b,y>-g(y), with X={x in R^n:||x||<=RX}, Y={y in R^m:||y||<=RY}, Euclidean norms, spectral matrix norm, g=0, and convex quadratic f. Define phi(x)=f(x)+max_{y in Y}<Ax-b,y> and psi(y)=min_{x in X}(f(x)+<Ax-b,y>). Set k=2t+4, RX=sqrt(k)(2k+1), RY=sqrt(k)/2. The R^m dual space follows Eq. (1); Eq. (88)'s printed R^n is explicitly noted as a dimensional inconsistency.
statement.parameter_domains: m,n,t in positive integers; 8<m<=n; 1<=t<m/4-2; Lf>0; LA in [0,Lf]; k=2t+4; RX^2=k(2k+1)^2; RY^2=k/4.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each admissible m,n,t,Lf,LA and each deterministic method M of Eq. (8), there exists an instance with convex quadratic f, grad f Lipschitz with constant at most Lf, ||A||=LA, g=0 and the specified balls, on which its feasible output at index t satisfies the conclusion. The instance may depend on M and t. No randomized guarantee or common instance for all methods is asserted.
